checks: For t≤0 the triangle lies in every cap. For t≥r/2 the equal normal leaves a set of zero planar area, with the closed hypotenuse included at equality. Scaling by r multiplies area by r², so the normalized unit-triangle fractions in the proof give exactly area/V.

Coordinate exchange covers the full simplex of normals, including its axis endpoints. For 0<θ<1/2 the lower-threshold branch removes the origin triangle and the other branch keeps the e₁ triangle. The products of edge fractions give the stated two rational functions. At α=1−θ the line passes through e₂ and both formulas agree; each denominator is positive in its assigned range.

On [1/2,1−θ], α(1−α) decreases, so 1−θ²/[α(1−α)] is nonincreasing. The derivative in α of the second branch has numerator (α−θ)[α(4θ−1)−θ] over the positive squared denominator. If 4θ−1≤0 the bracket is negative; if 1/4<θ≤1/3 its maximum is at α=1 and is 3θ−1≤0. Thus α=1 attains the global minimum through θ=1/3.

For 1/3<θ<1/2 the stationary point θ/(4θ−1) lies in the second branch since its excess over 1−θ is (1−2θ)²/(4θ−1)>0, and it is below 1. The first derivative changes from negative to positive there and substitution gives 4θ(1−2θ). The branches agree at t=0,r/3,r/2. Monotonicity gives the lower bound 4r²/9 for every t≤r/3 and equality at the interface.

Independently expanded the derivative and evaluated the stationary point symbolically over QQ in SageMath 10.8. Exact polyhedral clipping and volume over QQ checked the lower envelope against 1,161 sampled normal/radius/threshold combinations, including attained minima with axis, equal, and interior optimizing normals and closed support endpoints. These checks accompany the analytic minimization.

At (t,t) it yields 4t² in units of V for 0<t<r/3, whereas the restricted minimum in this draft is (r−t)². The upper positive branch agrees numerically with the ordinary depth, but the accepted fact does not give the full restricted envelope.
Its balanced-barycentric simplex formula covers ordinary depth at (t,t) for r/3≤t≤r/2, with value 4t(r−2t) in units of V, and also the centroid. It does not give the restricted branch for t<r/3.

The paired-chain proof uses the same upper-threshold polynomial as a lower bound on a different mixed-integer problem with reflection pairs. It does not assert the sharp restricted envelope over all thresholds.
